Context/Background:
Circular RNA (circRNA) is a class of noncoding RNA with regulatory potentials. Here, we identified circRMST as an exceptionally abundant circRNA predominantly expressed in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with strong conservation between humans and mice.

To explore the functional role of circRMST, we designed two shRNAs targeting the backspliced junction (BSJ), achieving 70%–93% knockdown efficiency. In 3D Matrigel-embedded cultures, circRMST knockdown significantly impaired cell growth across three NEPC and four SCLC-A models. Additionally, cell cycle analysis in SHP77 cells revealed cell-cycle arrest. In vivo, SHP77 xenografts in NSG immunodeficient mice exhibited markedly reduced tumor growth upon circRMST depletion.
Prompt:
To investigate transcriptional changes following circRMST knockdown, we performed RNA-seq in SHP77 cells and identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes.

What are the most relevant pathways in a GSEA results with the differential gene list?  Nominate a target most relevant for neuroendocrine prostate cancer.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
CircRMST is a highly abundant circular RNA in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small‐cell lung cancer (SCLC), with 70–93% knockdown achieved by two BSJ‐targeting shRNAs in SHP77 NEPC cells. 3D Matrigel cultures and in vivo xenografts demonstrated growth impairment and cell‐cycle arrest upon circRMST depletion. RNA-seq of shRNA1 vs shRNA2 knockdowns in SHP77 cells yielded ~9,000 DE genes (padj < 0.05), including loss of NE lineage drivers (ASCL1, GRP) and induction of stress/metabolic regulators (SESN3, FTH1).  

Keywords  
• circRMST  
• Neuroendocrine cell cycle  
• mTORC1 signaling  
• Mitotic spindle  
• Neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction  

Candidate Genes  
PLK1, MTOR, HSPA5, SESN3, SSTR3, ASCL1  

Pathway Enrichments  
The preranked GSEA (log2FC ranking) returned the following overall up/down ratios and top terms:

• KEGG_2016: 6 up/11 down (35%/65%, ratio 0.55)  
• GO_Biological_Process_2023: 236 up/113 down (68%/32%, ratio 2.09)  
• Reactome_Pathways_2024: 93 up/52 down (64%/36%, ratio 1.79)  
• MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 12 up/1 down (92%/8%, ratio 12)

| Hypoxia (NES 1.971)              | Up        | HSPA5, ERRFI1, BHLHE40, IL6, DDIT4, … |

Analysis  
Across libraries, metabolic/ER stress programs and cell-cycle machinery were prominently upregulated upon circRMST knockdown, whereas neuroactive ligand-receptor modules were downregulated. MSigDB Hallmark showed the strongest bias toward upregulated programs (92% up, ratio 12), led by mTORC1 activation and spindle assembly, consistent with cell-cycle perturbation. KEGG pathways related to neurotransmission (e.g., “Neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction”) were among the most repressed. The integrated GSEA highlights mTORC1 signaling and mitotic regulators as key axes.  

Targeted Subset (keyword-guided)  
• mTORC1 signaling (MSigDB_Hallmark_2020; NES 2.836, FDR 0.137): leading-edge genes include CCT6A, HSPA5, ACLY, AURKA, PLK1  
• Mitotic cell-cycle:  
  – GO: Positive regulation of G1/S transition (NES 2.318; genes ANXA1, RDX, PLCB1, STOX1)  
  – Reactome: Mitotic G2–G2 M phases (NES 1.964; genes PSMD1, UBB, WEE1, PLK1, CDKN1A)  
  – Hallmark: Mitotic spindle (NES 2.622; genes KIF22, BUB1, AURKA, PLK1, CLASP1)  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  
Up-regulated:  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                             | Pathway(s)                 |
|--------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| PLK1   | Up        | Polo-like kinase 1; mitotic kinase        | Mitotic spindle; G2-M       |
| MTOR   | Up        | Ser/Thr kinase; central mTORC1 component  | mTORC1 signaling            |

Down-regulated:  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                             | Pathway(s)                                    |
|--------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| SSTR3  | Down      | Somatostatin receptor 3; GPCR             | Neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction        |

Comparisons  
The consistent upregulation of cell‐cycle regulators (PLK1, AURKA) across Reactome and Hallmark contrasts with the downregulation of neuroendocrine receptors (SSTR3) in KEGG. This suggests circRMST knockdown shifts SHP77 cells from a neuroendocrine phenotype toward a stressed, cell‐cycle-arrested state.  

Implications  
PLK1 emerges as a mechanistic vulnerability: its inhibition could synergize with circRMST targeting to enforce mitotic arrest and apoptosis in NEPC. Concomitant mTORC1 activation implies metabolic stress that might be exploited by dual PLK1/mTOR inhibitors.  

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate PLK1 protein activity (phospho-PLK1) and test PLK1 inhibitors in circRMST-depleted SHP77 cells.  
2. Assess mTORC1 downstream signaling (p-S6K) to confirm GSEA predictions.  
3. Examine electrophysiological or ligand-binding assays for SSTR3 to gauge functional loss of neuroendocrine signaling.  
4. Clarify whether UPR/ER stress (HSPA5 induction) contributes to cell-cycle arrest via co-treatment with chemical chaperones.  

References  
None.
